title: StochasticConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean

problem_class.label: other
problem_class.details: Constrained monotone variational inequality: find x*∈X with ⟨F(x*),w−x*⟩≥0 for every w∈X. X is convex and F is globally continuous and monotone. No objective function, strong monotonicity, or bounded feasible-set diameter is assumed.

oracle.label: proximal
oracle.details: Oracle 1 returns the exact Euclidean projection onto X, characterized by proj(z)∈X and ⟨z−proj(z),w−proj(z)⟩≤0 for every w∈X. Projection calls and stochastic operator calls have separately capped, fixed budgets.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and Convergence; supplied extracted budgets.

oracle.label: other
oracle.details: Oracle 0 returns a single stochastic operator evaluation g(x,ω), with E[g(x,ω)]=F(x) and E[‖g(x,ω)−F(x)‖²]≤σ². Seeds are IID across calls; samples cannot be requested again at another point. F need not be a gradient.

distinctive_assumptions.label: generalized_smoothness
distinctive_assumptions.details: For every x,y and every M bounding ‖F(x+θ(y−x))‖ over θ∈[0,1], ‖F(x)−F(y)‖≤(L0+L1M)‖x−y‖. Here L0>0 and L1≥0; a global Lipschitz constant is not required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: Uniform central second-moment bound σ² with σ≥0, unbiasedness, joint measurability, and integrability. No bounded-sample or exponential-tail assumption is imposed.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, with completeness and its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The public input includes E, x0, L0, L1, R, G, σ, ε, δ and the sampling type. R>0, G≥0, ε>0, and 0<δ<1. There exists a hidden solution x*∈X with ‖x0−x*‖≤R and ‖F(x*)‖≤G; x0∈X. F, X, the solution, and the sampling law are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/StochasticConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone.lean: Params, Instance, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid, and spec.admissible.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output must belong to X on the same success event as the residual guarantee.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Joint feasibility and residual accuracy hold with probability at least 1−δ over algorithm and oracle randomness.

accuracy.label: other
accuracy.details: The measurable output x must admit ξ∈N_X(x) such that ‖F(x)+ξ‖≤ε, where N_X(x)={ξ: ⟨ξ,w−x⟩≤0 for every w∈X}. This is an unsquared normal-cone residual criterion; ξ need not be returned.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The monotone variational-inequality formulation combines operator-dependent generalized smoothness, potentially unbounded constraints, bounded-variance stochastic evaluations, and a high-probability normal-cone residual requirement. This classification does not establish novelty.

descriptionHtml:
Stochastic Constrained Monotone Inclusions

We consider a variational inequality for a continuous monotone operator F:E→E on a convex set X in a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space E. The operator satisfies a segmentwise generalized Lipschitz bound with constants L0>0 and L1≥0. A given x0∈X lies within distance R>0 of a solution x⋆ with ∥F(x⋆)∥≤G, where G≥0. Two oracles return independent unbiased estimates of F(x) with variance at most σ2, where σ≥0, and exact projections onto X. For ε>0 and δ∈(0,1), the goal is a feasible output x¯ admitting a normal vector v, meaning ⟨v,w−x¯⟩≤0 for all w∈X, with ∥F(x¯)+v∥≤ε, with probability at least 1−δ.

The variational inequality is to find x⋆∈X such that ⟨F(x⋆),w−x⋆⟩≥0for every w∈X. The norm is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, the measurable sample space Ω, x0, and the parameters L0,L1,R,G,σ,ε,δ; it accesses F and X through the two oracles. Both oracles accept queries at any point of E, and their calls are counted separately.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Constraint set and nearby solution). The set X is convex and contains x0. There exists a solution x⋆ of the variational inequality satisfying ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R,∥F(x⋆)∥≤G. The projection oracle returns ΠX(z) at z∈E, where ΠX(z)∈X,⟨z−ΠX(z),w−ΠX(z)⟩≤0for every w∈X.

Assumption 2 (Monotonicity and generalized Lipschitz continuity). The operator F is continuous on E and satisfies ⟨F(x)−F(y),x−y⟩≥0for all x,y∈E. For all x,y∈E and M∈R, the segment bound ∥F(x+θ(y−x))∥≤Mfor every θ∈[0,1] implies ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1M)∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Stochastic operator oracle). There is a probability measure ν on Ω and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable and ∥g(x,⋅)−F(x)∥2 is integrable under ν, with EZ∼ν[g(x,Z)]=F(x),EZ∼ν[∥g(x,Z)−F(x)∥2]≤σ2. Let (Zk)k≥0 be measurable, mutually independent samples with common law ν, independent of the algorithm’s randomness. At the kth call across both oracles, a stochastic operator query at x returns g(x,Zk), while a projection query returns ΠX(x).

The output x¯∈E must be measurable. For x∈X, define the normal cone NX(x)={v∈E:⟨v,w−x⟩≤0 for every w∈X}. The required accuracy is P(x¯∈X and ∃v∈NX(x¯):∥F(x¯)+v∥≤ε)≥1−δ, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the independent sample sequence.

comparisonHtml:
A finite-dimensional real inner-product space; convex X with exact projection and x0∈X; continuous, globally monotone F satisfying ∥F(x)−F(y)∥≤(L0+L1supz∈[x,y]∥F(z)∥)∥x−y∥. A VI solution x⋆∈X satisfies ∥x0−x⋆∥≤R and ∥F(x⋆)∥≤G. Jointly measurable, integrable stochastic evaluations satisfy ∫g(x,ω)dp=F(x) and ∫∥g(x,ω)−F(x)∥2dp≤σ2, with IID samples of law p under P. Public parameters satisfy L0,R,ε>0, L1,G,σ≥0, 0<δ<1. Target: a measurable output Y with P{Y∈X, ∃v∈NX(Y):∥F(Y)+v∥≤ε}≥1−δ. Costs count all operator samples plus projections.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedMonotone
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Basic

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.StochasticConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone

open OracleTemplate

structure Params extends StochasticGeneralizedMonotone.Params.{0} where
  G : ℝ

structure Instance (q : Params) where
  F : q.E → q.E
  X : Set q.E

abbrev spec : Setup where
  numOracles := 2
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance := Instance
  Query q := q.E
  Reply q := q.E
  Output q := q.E
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.L0 ∧ 0 ≤ q.L1 ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.G ∧ 0 ≤ q.σ ∧
    0 < q.ε ∧ 0 < q.δ ∧ q.δ < 1
  admissible q I O :=
    ∃ (g : q.E → q.Ω → q.E) (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)) (proj : q.E → q.E),
    LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k)
      (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (i, x) seed => if i = 0 then g x seed else proj x } ∧
    (∀ z, proj z ∈ I.X ∧ ∀ w ∈ I.X, ⟪z - proj z, w - proj z⟫ ≤ 0) ∧
    Convex ℝ I.X ∧ q.x0 ∈ I.X ∧ Continuous I.F ∧
    (∀ x y, 0 ≤ ⟪I.F x - I.F y, x - y⟫) ∧
    (∀ x y M, (∀ θ ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ‖I.F (x + θ • (y - x))‖ ≤ M) →
      ‖I.F x - I.F y‖ ≤ (q.L0 + q.L1 * M) * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ I.X, (∀ w ∈ I.X, 0 ≤ ⟪I.F xstar, w - xstar⟫) ∧
      ‖q.x0 - xstar‖ ≤ q.R ∧ ‖I.F xstar‖ ≤ q.G) ∧
    StochasticGeneralizedMonotone.IsStochasticOperator (p : Measure _) I.F g q.σ
  successful q I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ (P : Measure _) {ω | ¬(output ω ∈ I.X ∧
      ∃ ξ : q.E, (∀ w ∈ I.X, ⟪ξ, w - output ω⟫ ≤ 0) ∧ ‖I.F (output ω) + ξ‖ ≤ q.ε)} ≤
        ENNReal.ofReal q.δ

end LongTails.Setups.StochasticConstrainedGeneralizedMonotone
